data.name: Reuel
data.gender_notes: Reuel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Reuel's name is derived from the Hebrew word 'ראואל' (rēʾûʾāl), which means 'friend of God'. In the Bible, Reuel appears as the name of an Midianite priest and the father of Jethro, who was Moses' father-in-law. The name Reuel carries the meaning “God is my friend” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Reuel usually hope their child will grow to embody god is my friend and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies faith and companionship with God.
data.etymology: Reuel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is my friend.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Reuel total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: רואל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רואל הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא המראה שלי' או 'חברו של אלוהים'. השם מורכב מ'רא' שמשמעותו 'לראות' ו'אל' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם נמצא בספר בראשית ובספר שמות, ומתייחס לאחד מבניו של ישמעאל ואחד מהאבות של העם האדומי.

in_greek.name: Ρουήλ
in_greek.meaning: Ρουήλ - Ο Θεός είναι το φως μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Ρουήλ είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι το φως μου' ή 'Φίλος του Θεού'. Το όνομα αποτελείται από το 'Ρα' που σημαίνει 'να βλέπω' και το 'Ελ' που σημαίνει 'Θεός'. Στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ματθαίου, ο Ρουήλ αναφέρεται ως πρόγονος του Ιησού Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Reuel
in_latin.long_meaning: Reuel est nomen hebraicum quod significat 'Deus est lux mea' vel 'Amicus Dei'. Nomen componitur ex 'Ra' quod significat 'videre' et 'El' quod significat 'Deus'. In ecclesia primitiva, nomen Reuel habebat significationem spiritualem et mysticam, et referebatur ad unum de filiis Ismaelis et ad patrem populi Edomitarum.

in_english.name: Reuel
in_english.meaning: God is my sight or friend of God
in_english.long_meaning: Reuel is a Christian name with Hebrew origins, meaning 'God is my sight' or 'friend of God'. It is derived from the Hebrew words 'ra' (to see) and 'el' (God). Reuel appears in the Bible as the name of one of Ishmael's sons and a forefather of the Edomites. In Christian tradition, the name Reuel symbolizes spiritual insight and a deep connection with God. It is associated with qualities such as wisdom, intuition, and leadership.

data.cultural_impact: Historically, the name Reuel has been associated with Israelite and Midianite culture, as it was borne by a significant figure in the Old Testament. Reuel, as a Midianite priest, represents the merging of two distinct cultural influences - Israelite and Midianite - and signifies the religious connections between the two peoples.
data.spiritual_significance: Etymologically, the name Reuel signifies a 'friend of God'. In a spiritual context, this name implies a deep connection with the divine providence and a commitment to living a life rooted in faith and devotion to God. As such, Reuel is an inspiring name for those who value their faith and seek to deepen their spiritual connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Reuel, meaning "Friend of God", symbolizes the deep bond and companionship between an individual and the divine presence. It is a reminder that God is not a distant deity, but a loving friend who is always there in times of need. Embracing this name encourages a life of devotion and fellowship with the divine.

biblical_reference.note: Reuel is mentioned as one of the sons of Ishmael and as a leader of the tribe of Reuben.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Reuel the Midianite prophet who interceded for Hagar and Ishmael. (Genesis 21:16-18) The name Reuel carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Abraham's servant Eliezer goes to find a wife for his master's son Isaac. Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian slave, gives birth to Ishmael, and Sarah casts her out with her son. God hears the cry of the boy and sends an angel to comfort Hagar. The angel tells Hagar to name the boy Ishmael, meaning 'God hears'. Hagar then goes to the well of Beer-lahai-roi, where she meets Reuel, the Midianite, who offers her and Ishmael water. Reuel prays for them and God hears and grants his prayer, ensuring their survival in the wilderness.

historical_references.reference: Reuel, son of Hasadiah, who was a Levite and a seer during the reign of King Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 26:22)
historical_references.context: Hezekiah was a king of Judah who did what was right in the eyes of the Lord. Hezekiah's military successes brought great wealth and prestige to Jerusalem. But Hezekiah's pride caused him to seek an alliance with Babylon's King Sennacherib. When Sennacherib invaded Judah, Hezekiah's trusted advisor Isaiah prophesied that the Lord would deliver Jerusalem. Reuel, along with other prophets, spoke in the name of the Lord, and Hezekiah was encouraged and strengthened by their words.
